title: Eventual injectivity and flat cokernels at Noetherian local arrow stages
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set. For each $i\in I$ let $\varphi_i:R_i\to S_i$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be another such homomorphism. Here local means that the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. For $i\le j$ let $r_{ji}:R_i\to R_j$ and $s_{ji}:S_i\to S_j$ be local homomorphisms, with local cocone maps $r_i:R_i\to R$ and $s_i:S_i\to S$. All ring squares commute, transitions are identities at equal indices and respect composition, and the cocones are compatible. Suppose $R=\varinjlim R_i$ and $S=\varinjlim S_i$ as rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. These colimits are algebraic: elements come from stages and equality is detected at a common later stage. Put $\mathfrak m_i=\mathfrak m_{R_i}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R$, $k_i=R_i/\mathfrak m_i$, and $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Assume $R_i,S_i$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $M_i,N_i$ be finite $S_i$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $u_i:M_i\to N_i$ be $S_i$-linear. Give them additive semilinear transitions $m_{ji},n_{ji}$ over $s_{ji}$, and additive semilinear cocones $\mu_i:M_i\to M$, $\nu_i:N_i\to N$ over $s_i$, where $M,N$ are $S$-modules and $u:M\to N$ is $S$-linear. Transitions respect identities and composition, cocones are compatible, $n_{ji}u_i=u_jm_{ji}$, and $\nu_i u_i=u\mu_i$. Suppose $M,N$ are the algebraic colimits of the underlying abelian groups, with their induced $S$-actions. Suppose for every $i\le j$ the canonical map $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ is a localization at a multiplicative subset (all denominators become units, every target element is a fraction, and an element mapping to zero is killed by a denominator), and the canonical maps $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\to M_j$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a m_{ji}(x)$, and $N_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\to N_j$, $y\otimes a\mapsto a n_{ji}(y)$, are isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Assume $N$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and the induced map $\overline u:M/\mathfrak mM\to N/\mathfrak mN$ is injective. Assume there is $i_1$ such that the map $\Psi_j:(M_j/\mathfrak m_jM_j)\otimes_{k_j}k\to M/\mathfrak mM$, $[x]\otimes c\mapsto c[\mu_j(x)]$, is injective for every $j\ge i_1$. Then there exists $i_2\ge i_1$ such that for every $j\ge i_2$, the module $N_j$ is flat over $R_j$, the induced map $\overline{u_j}:M_j/\mathfrak m_jM_j\to N_j/\mathfrak m_jN_j$ is injective, $u_j$ is injective, and $C_j=N_j/u_j(M_j)$ is flat over $R_j$. No injectivity hypothesis is imposed on the cocone map $N_j/\mathfrak m_jN_j\to N/\mathfrak mN$. All sets and objects may be placed in one common sufficiently large universe.

proof.text: Bundle the target modules and additive transition maps as a functor D. The supplied representatives and eventual equality identify its cocone with the filtered colimit in sets, hence in abelian groups. Identify the categorical ring colimits with the supplied colimit cocones. The ring and additive equivalences respect scalar multiplication; [lem-pc-flat-semilinear-equiv] transports the assumed flatness of N. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat] to obtain a flat stage a. Mathlib supplies preservation of filtered ring colimits by the forgetful functor, so the additional elementwise ring-colimit hypotheses are unnecessary for this interface.

source.place: Tag 00R6 (lemma-colimit-eventually-flat), as used in the first paragraph of Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general)

proof.text: For any $j\ge a$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-another-variant-local-criterion] to the square $(R_a,S_a,R_j,S_j)$ and $I=0$. This is a proper ideal since $R_a$ is local. The quotient condition is precisely flatness of $N_a$ over $R_a$. The multiplication-kernel condition is automatic: $0\otimes_{R_a}N_a=0$, since every pure tensor has zero first factor. All four rings are Noetherian local, all four arrows are local, and the square and localization hypotheses are given. The criterion makes $N_a\otimes_{S_a}S_j$ flat over $R_j$; the specified base-change isomorphism identifies this module with $N_j$. Choose an upper bound $i_2$ of $a$ and $i_1$. Then $N_j$ is flat over $R_j$ for every $j\ge i_2$.

source.place: Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness), specialization I=0; eventual flatness assertion in the first paragraph of Tag 046Y

proof.text: Fix j above i₂. Locality gives the field algebra k_j → k. The stage fibre V_j = k_j tensor_(R_j) M_j is a vector space over k_j and therefore flat. Mathlib Module.Flat.tensorProduct_mk_injective gives injectivity of V_j → k tensor_(k_j) V_j, including V_j = 0; the field algebra is faithful. TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange identifies the codomain with k tensor_(R_j) M_j and sends 1 tensor (c tensor x) to image(c) tensor x, realizing [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. Composing this injection t with the assumed injective Ψ_j embeds the stage source fibre in the limit source fibre.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), final paragraph: the injectivity of the scalar-extended comparison implies that of the source fibre cocone

proof.text: The semilinear cocone ν_j and the induced residue-field map define β_j:k_j tensor_(R_j) N_j → k tensor_R N. On pure tensors the identity ν_j u_j = u μ_j proves the commuting square β_j ū_j = ū Ψ_j t; tensor induction extends it to all elements. Equality under ū_j therefore implies equality under Ψ_j t, by injectivity of the limit fibre arrow ū. Injectivity of Ψ_j and of t then proves injectivity of ū_j. No injectivity of β_j is used.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), final paragraph: the commutative fibre square

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-mod-injective] with its finite source $N$ equal to our $M_j$, its flat target $M$ equal to our $N_j$, and local ring map $R_j\to S_j$. The source is finite over the Noetherian local ring $S_j$ by hypothesis, the target is flat over $R_j$ by step 2, and the map is $R_j$-linear because it is $S_j$-linear. Step 4 supplies its residue-fibre injectivity. The criterion gives injectivity of $u_j$ and flatness of $N_j/u_j(M_j)$ over $R_j$. Together with steps 2 and 4 these are all four conclusions for every $j\ge i_2$.
